why: The model makes this **Ole Miss by 2.0**; Vegas has **Texas by 3.5**. That's a **5.5-point** gap in Ole Miss's favor.
Texas is the better team (#11 of 138 FBS overall vs. Ole Miss at #13 of 138 FBS), but the model sees a smaller gap than the 3.5-point line implies.

Play for play, Ole Miss's offense ranks #5 of 138 FBS in success rate and Texas's defense ranks #6 of 138 FBS at stopping it. (Success rate = share of plays that keep the offense on schedule; garbage time removed and adjusted for schedule.)
Ole Miss has played about 6 pts/game better over the last 3 weeks than its full-season rating.
Texas has played about 3 pts/game worse over the last 3 weeks than its full-season rating.
It's a conference game, where home field is worth only about 1.1 pts, so playing on the road costs Ole Miss less than usual.
The line has moved 5.0 pts toward Ole Miss since it opened (Texas -8.5 → Texas -3.5), so bettors are agreeing with the model.
watch: The model only sees points, yards and home field. It knows nothing about injuries, weather or motivation.
